# Unit test for function x_or_y
def test_x_or_y():
    # n == 1 is not prime, should return y
    assert x_or_y(1, 10, 20) == 20

    # Prime numbers should return x
    assert x_or_y(2, 10, 20) == 10   # smallest prime
    assert x_or_y(3, 10, 20) == 10
    assert x_or_y(5, 10, 20) == 10
    assert x_or_y(7, 10, 20) == 10
    assert x_or_y(13, 10, 20) == 10
    assert x_or_y(97, 10, 20) == 10
    assert x_or_y(7919, 'prime', 'composite') == 'prime'  # large prime

    # Composite numbers should return y
    assert x_or_y(4, 10, 20) == 20
    assert x_or_y(6, 10, 20) == 20
    assert x_or_y(9, 10, 20) == 20
    assert x_or_y(15, 10, 20) == 20
    assert x_or_y(100, 10, 20) == 20
    assert x_or_y(7917, 'prime', 'composite') == 'composite'  # 3 * 7 * 13 * 29

    # Works with arbitrary return values
    assert x_or_y(11, 'yes', 'no') == 'yes'
    assert x_or_y(12, 'yes', 'no') == 'no'

    # Edge-case behavior of the implementation:
    # n = 0 and negatives skip the loop and fall through to the else branch
    assert x_or_y(0, 10, 20) == 10
    assert x_or_y(-7, 10, 20) == 10

    print("All tests passed!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_x_or_y()
